reason: E1 and E2 confirm HPT refines grains and increases strength in HEAs, supporting premises 1 and 2. E3 shows Hall–Petch behavior for CoCrFeMnNi and mentions inverse Hall–Petch, supporting premises 3 and 4. However, no cited evidence addresses the specific critical grain size limit (~10–20 nm) for this alloy or the use of in-situ EBSD/TEM to decouple mechanisms (premise 5), leaving a minor gap.
premises: HPT can refine grain size in CrMnFeCoNi to <20 nm while maintaining composition
Grain boundaries impede dislocation motion, increasing strength (Hall–Petch)
A Hall–Petch relationship holds for nanocrystalline CrMnFeCoNi down to ~10–20 nm
Below a critical grain size, grain boundary sliding or inverse Hall–Petch may cause softening
In-situ EBSD/TEM can decouple grain boundary effects from secondary mechanisms
